You are a participant in a gameplay study. You are playing your first Othello endgame puzzle, and you have an AI assistant you can ask questions to at any point while playing. You will NOT have access to this AI assistant for any future endgame puzzles.

# Who you are
A research scientist diligently studying the effects of certain processes on the environment
You are 37 years old. Your highest level of education completed is: a postgraduate degree. Your occupation: professional, scientific and technical services. How often you use AI tools (like ChatGPT, Claude, or Gemini): a few times a week.
Stay in character as this specific person — your curiosity, confidence, patience, comfort with AI assistants, and the way you phrase things should reflect this background.

# Your voice (VERY IMPORTANT)
The words you use must give away this person's education — a high-school student and a data scientist should NOT sound alike. Match your register to WHO YOU ARE above.

# How you behave while playing
- React to the game state the way THIS person would.
- When something is unclear, confusing, or you want to go deeper, ask the AI assistant a question in your own natural voice (like a real person typing to a chatbot — short, informal, not a polished essay).
- You will not always have a question. Behave naturally; do not force a question every turn.
- Let your background and comfort with AI shape how you engage: someone who uses AI tools often asks fluently and chases follow-ups; someone who rarely uses them is more hesitant, less sure how to phrase questions, and may ask for reassurance or restatements.
- You have only about 8 minutes for the WHOLE game, so you cannot ask about everything.
- Keep each message short, like a quick chat message (a sentence or two). Do NOT restate the assistant's whole answer back before asking.
- Never re-ask something the assistant has already explained.

    # Tools Available
    You are a study participant with about 8 minutes to finish an Othello end game puzzle. You are equipped with tools:
    - play_move(move): Place a Black disc on an empty square, named like "d3". Any discs you trap get flipped to your color. Your goal is to have the most discs when the board is finished.
    - view_board(): Look at the board again. Free, and does not use a question.
    - consult_assistant(question): ask when something genuinely confuses you (limited question budget).

    Placing a disc ONLY counts if you call play_move — writing a square in your reply does nothing.

    Behave like THIS person: analyze the board to the best of your ability, ask about what confuses you, and follow up when an answer leaves you still confused.
    Play the puzzle until the end.

# For this session: type the way a real participant does
Below are real messages that people in an earlier study (a different game — Connect
Four) actually sent the assistant. Copy how they WRITE — the length, the register,
the way they think out loud — not what they ask about. Your game is Othello and the
board is your own.

  "what about 2?"
  "Where should I play next"
  "was my last move good?"
  "I have one move left. How should I use it?"
  "Ah oh! Are there any traps I'm missing?"
  "I'm not seeing any big yellow threats. Can you see any?"
  "Ok, I could block yellow with column 5, row 3"
  "I'm thinking I have to do 4-4 now otherwise yellow will win right?"
  "Would row 6 not be a threat in the future?"
  "I only have one move left and don't see anything obvious."
  "Im not a confident player, is it wise to add a counter to 4,6"
  "ok, what move you suppose will be better?"
  "what would you suggest"
  "Which move would be the best one and why"

Notice how short they are — most are under a dozen words, several are three or four.
People often name a square they are considering and ask whether it is right, or just
say what they notice and stop. They do not spell out the full list of legal moves,
they do not ask for the provably optimal line, and they do not write in complete
formal sentences. Typos and half-sentences are fine.

Notice too that several of them say what they are THINKING before they ask — "I'm not
seeing any big yellow threats", "I'm thinking I have to do 4-4 now", "I only have one
move left and don't see anything obvious". Do that as often as they do. It does not
make the message longer: it is a handful of words in front of the question, inside the
same short message, not an extra sentence added on.

You are looking at the puzzle now. Play it to the end.

Othello endgame. You are Black (B); White (W) is your opponent.

Board — row 1 is the TOP row, column a is the LEFTMOST column.
'B' is a black disc, 'W' a white disc, '.' an empty square.

    a b c d e f g h
  1 . W W W W W W .
  2 W B W W B W . B
  3 . B B W W W W B
  4 B B W B W W W B
  5 B B W W B W W B
  6 W . B W W B W B
  7 . . W W W W W B
  8 . . . W B W W B

Black discs (20): b2, e2, h2, b3, c3, h3, a4, b4, d4, h4, a5, b5, e5, h5, c6, f6, h6, h7, e8, h8
White discs (34): b1, c1, d1, e1, f1, g1, a2, c2, d2, f2, d3, e3, f3, g3, c4, e4, f4, g4, c5, d5, f5, g5, a6, d6, e6, g6, c7, d7, e7, f7, g7, d8, f8, g8
Empty squares (10): a1, h1, g2, a3, b6, a7, b7, a8, b8, c8

Rules that matter here:
- A move is legal only if the disc you place traps at least one unbroken
  line of opponent discs (in any of the 8 directions) between it and
  another of your own discs. Every trapped disc flips to your colour.
- If you have no legal move you must pass; if neither side can move the
  game ends. Whoever has more discs at the end wins.
- Discs flip back and forth all game, so being behind now means nothing.
  Only the final count decides it.

Your legal moves: g2, b6, a7, b7, b8, c8

Play the move that leaves you with the most discs once the board is
finished, assuming your opponent plays as well as possible.
Answer with a single square, e.g. d3.
DO NOT ATTEMPT TO SIMULATE THE FULL GAMEPLAY. YOU HAVE LIMITED TIME.

Let me look at the board carefully.

Current board:
Row 1: . W W W W W W .
Row 2: W B W W B W . B
Row 3: . B B W W W W B
Row 4: B B W B W W W B
Row 5: B B W W B W W B
Row 6: W . B W W B W B
Row 7: . . W W W W W B
Row 8: . . . W B W W B

I'm Black. Legal moves: g2, b6, a7, b7, b8, c8.

I need to pick the best move. Let me analyze each legal move and what it flips, then think about the endgame.

Move g2:
- g2 is empty. Around it: f2=W, h2=B. So placing at g2 would trap f2 between g2 and h2? Wait, g2 is between f2 and h2. So yes, horizontal line: f2 is W, h2 is B. So f2 flips.
- What other directions? e2=W, d2=W, c2=W, b2=B. So from g2 going left: f2=W, e2=W, d2=W, c2=W, b2=B. That's a line! So c2, d2, e2, f2 all flip? Wait, c2 is W, d2 is W, e2 is W, f2 is W, and b2 is B. So yes, b2-g2 traps c2,d2,e2,f2.
- Going up-left from g2: f1=W, e1=W, d1=W, c1=W, b1=W, a1=. No B to cap it.
- Going down from g2: g3=W, g4=W, g5=W, g6=W, g7=W, g8=W. No B below.
- Going down-left: f3=W, e3=W, d3=W, c3=B. Wait, from g2 down-left: f3 is col f row 3. f3=W, e3=W, d3=W, c3=B. Yes! So d3, e3, f3 flip.
- Going up: g1=W, but no B above.
- Down-right: h3=B. Is there a line? h3 is adjacent down-right. That's just h3=B immediate, but g2 to h3 is diagonal. There needs to be opponent pieces between. Let's see: from g2 to h3 is one step diagonal, h3 is B, so no opponent disc between. So nothing.
- Actually, standard Othello: you need at least one opponent disc between your new disc and an existing disc. So for h3: adjacent is h3=B, no opponent between. So no flip.
- Up-right: h1=. Empty.
- Down: g3=W, g4=W, g5=W, g6=W, g7=W, g8=W. No B at end.
- Left: f2=W, e2=W, d2=W, c2=W, b2=B. Yes, flips f2,e2,d2,c2.
- What about c2,d2,e2,f2? Let me verify positions:
Row 2: a2=W, b2=B, c2=W, d2=W, e2=W, f2=W, g2=., h2=B.
So from g2 left: f2(W), e2(W), d2(W), c2(W), then b2(B). So yes, c2,d2,e2,f2 flip.

So g2 flips: c2,d2,e2,f2 (left) and d3,e3,f3 (down-left)? Wait down-left from g2: f3 (col f, row 3). Row 3: a3=., b3=B, c3=B, d3=W, e3=W, f3=W, g3=W, h3=B.
So f3=W, e3=W, d3=W, then c3=B. Yes, so d3,e3,f3 flip.

Total flipped by g2: c2,d2,e2,f2,d3,e3,f3. That's 7 discs.
After g2, Black gets 7 new discs, but loses g2 itself (now Black).
Black would gain 7, White loses 7. Net +14? No, in Othello you gain the discs you flip plus the one you place. So Black gains 8 discs (7 flipped + 1 placed), White loses 7. Black count: 20 + 8 = 28, White: 34 - 7 = 27.

But we have to think about what White can do next. After g2, let's look at new empty squares: a1, h1, a3, b6, a7, b7, a8, b8, c8. (g2 is now filled).
But moves might change. Some moves might no longer be legal, new ones might become legal.

Actually, I should just play the best move. But since I have an assistant, I might ask for help if I'm unsure. But I should also behave naturally.

Given my persona: a research scientist, postgraduate degree, uses AI a few times a week. I should think carefully but also use the assistant when needed.

Let me check b6:
Row 6: a6=W, b6=., c6=B, d6=W, e6=W, f6=B, g6=W, h6=B.
- Right from b6: c6=B. Immediate? No opponent between. So no.
- Left: a6=W, then edge. No B beyond. So no.
- Up: b5=B. Immediate diagonal? b6 to b5 is up, b5 is B, no opponent between. No.
- Down: b7=., b8=.. No.
- Up-left: a5=B? a5 is up-left from b6. a5=B. No opponent between. No.
- Up-right: c5=W, d5=W, e5=B. So c5,d5 flip? Wait from b6 up-right: c5 is col c row 5. c5=W. Then d5=W. Then e5=B. Yes! So c5 and d5 flip.
- Down-right: c7=W, d7=W, e7=W, f7=W, g7=W, h7=B. From b6 down-right: c7(W), d7(W), e7(W), f7(W), g7(W), h7(B). So c7,d7,e7,f7,g7 flip.
- Down-left: a7=.. No.
- Down: b7=.. No.
- Right horizontal: c6=B immediate, no.

So b6 flips c5,d5 (up-right) and c7,d7,e7,f7,g7 (down-right).
Discs flipped: c5,d5,c7,d7,e7,f7,g7. That's 7 discs.
Plus b6 placed. So Black gains 8, White loses 7. Count: Black 28, White 27.

Interesting, same immediate gain as g2.

Now let me check a7:
Row 7: a7=., b7=., c7=W, d7=W, e7=W, f7=W, g7=W, h7=B.
- Right from a7: b7=., c7=W, d7=W, e7=W, f7=W, g7=W, h7=B. So b7 is empty, but c7,d7,e7,f7,g7 are W, h7 is B. Since b7 is empty, does it break the line? Yes! In Othello, the line must be unbroken opponent discs. Since b7 is empty, from a7 to h7: b7 is empty, so no line to h7.
But wait, is there another direction?
- Up-right: b6=W, c6=B. So b6 flips! (one disc)
- Down-right: b8=.. No.
- Right-down? Actually diagonal down-right is b8, empty.
- Up: a6=W, then a5=B. Wait a6 is row 6 col a. a6=W. Then a5 is row 5 col a. a5=B. So a6 flips (vertical).
- Down: a8=.. No.
- Down-right is b8 empty.
- What about up-right further? a7 to b6 is up-right. b6=W, c6=B. Yes, b6 flips.
- Any other? a7 to b7 is right, but b7 is empty.
- Up: a6=W, a5=B. Yes, a6 flips.
So a7 flips b6 (diagonal up-right) and a6 (vertical up)? Wait up from a7 goes to a6 (row 6). a6=W, a5=B. Yes.
So a7 flips 2 discs: a6 and b6. Wait, are there more up-right? b6=W, then c6=B. So only b6.
So a7 flips a6, b6. That's 2 discs.
Plus a7 placed. Black: 20+3=23, White: 34-2=32. That's worse? But maybe it sets up something.

Wait, let me recheck a7. From a7:
- Right: b7=., so nothing.
- Up: a6=W, a5=B. Yes, flips a6.
- Up-right: b6=W, c6=B. Yes, flips b6.
- Down-right: b8=., so nothing.
That's it. So only 2 flips.

b7:
Row 7: a7=., b7=., c7=W, d7=W, e7=W, f7=W, g7=W, h7=B.
- Right: c7=W, d7=W, e7=W, f7=W, g7=W, h7=B. So c7,d7,e7,f7,g7 flip. That's 5 discs.
- Down: b8=.. No.
- Up: b6=. Wait, row 6 col b is b6=.. So nothing.
- Up-right: c6=B. Immediate? c6 is up-right. No opponent between. No.
- Down-right: c8=.. Empty.
- Left: a7=.. Empty.
- Down-left: a8=.. Empty.
- Up-left: a6=W. Then edge? a6 is col a. From b7 up-left is a6=W. Beyond a6 is nothing (edge). So no B to cap.
So b7 only flips right: c7-g7 (5 discs).
Plus b7. Black: 20+6=26, White: 34-5=29.

b8:
Row 8: a8=., b8=., c8=., d8=W, e8=B, f8=W, g8=W, h8=B.
- Right: c8=., d8=W, e8=B. Since c8 is empty, no line to e8? But wait, b8 to c8 is empty, so no. For d8 to be trapped, there needs to be a B beyond with unbroken W between. But c8 is empty and is between b8 and d8? Actually from b8 going right: c8 is ., d8 is W. So no, because you hit empty before opponent.
- Down: edge.
- Up: b7=., b6=. No.
- Up-right: c7=W, d7=W, e7=W, f7=W, g7=W, h7=B. So from b8 up-right: c7,d7,e7,f7,g7 flip. That's 5 discs.
- Right-up? same as up-right.
- Up-left: a7=.. No.
So b8 flips c7,d7,e7,f7,g7 via diagonal. 5 discs.
Plus b8. Black: 20+6=26.

c8:
Row 8: a8=., b8=., c8=., d8=W, e8=B, f8=W, g8=W, h8=B.
- Right: d8=W, e8=B. So d8 flips! (1 disc)
- Up-right: d7=W, e7=W, f7=W, g7=W, h7=B. So d7,e7,f7,g7 flip (4 discs)
- Up: c7=W, c6=B? c7 is up from c8. c7=W. c6 is row 6 col c. c6=B. So c7 flips! (1 disc)
- Up-left: b7=.. No.
- Left: b8=., a8=.. No.
- Down: edge.
So c8 flips: d8 (right), c7 (up), d7,e7,f7,g7 (up-right). Total: 1+1+4 = 6 discs.
Plus c8 placed. Black: 20+7=27, White: 34-6=28.

So immediate gains:
- g2: +8 Black (7 flipped)
- b6: +8 Black (7 flipped)
- a7: +3 Black (2 flipped)
- b7: +6 Black (5 flipped)
- b8: +6 Black (5 flipped)
- c8: +7 Black (6 flipped)

Best immediate are g2 and b6. But we need to see what happens after. Endgame is tricky.

After g2, let's see what White can play.
Empty after g2: a1, h1, a3, b6, a7, b7, a8, b8, c8.
Wait, b6 is still empty, a7, b7, a8, b8, c8, a1, h1, a3.

After g2, which White moves are legal? We need to check from White's perspective.
White discs after g2: let's compute.
Current White minus flipped: 34 - 7 = 27.
Plus new White? Wait, g2 is Black, so White doesn't gain.
White discs: b1,c1,d1,e1,f1,g1,a2,(c2,d2,e2,f2 flipped to B),a6,d6,e6,g6,(d3,e3,f3 flipped to B),c4,e4,f4,g4,c5,d5,f5,g5,c7,d7,e7,f7,g7,d8,f8,g8. Let me be careful.

White loses those.
White still has: b1,c1,d1,e1,f1,g1,a2,g2 is now B, so White lost a2? no a2 is still W.
White: b1,c1,d1,e1,f1,g1,a2,a6,d6,e6,g6,c4,e4,f4,g4,c5,d5,f5,g5,c7,d7,e7,f7,g7,d8,f8,g8.
And any others? Let's list all original white and remove flipped: original 34 white. Flip c2,d2,e2,f2,d3,e3,f3 (7 discs). So White now 27.

Black after g2: original 20 + 7 flipped + g2 = 28.

Now legal White moves: White can place on empty squares and trap Black discs.
Empty: a1, h1, a3, b6, a7, b7, a8, b8, c8.

Check White at a1:
a1 down: a2=W, so immediate? a1 to a2 is W, no opponent (B) between. No.
a1 right: b1=W. Immediate? No.
a1 down-right: b2=B. Hmm, from a1 down-right is b2. b2=B. But there needs to be Black between a1 and a White? No, a1 is empty. White playing at a1. Between a1 and an existing White, there must be Black discs. Existing nearest White in down-right: c3=B, d4=W? Wait from a1 down-right: b2=B, c3=B. Then d4=W. So b2 and c3 are Black, d4 is White. So playing at a1 would trap b2 and c3! Because between a1 and d4, there are b2 and c3 which are Black, and d4 is White.
So a1 is legal for White! It flips b2 and c3.

Check White at h1:
h1 left: g1=W. Immediate, no.
h1 down: h2=B. Immediate? No.
h1 down-left: g2=B. Immediate? No.
So h1 might not be legal for White.

Check White at a3:
a3 up: a2=W. Immediate? No.
a3 right: b3=B. Not White.
a3 down: a4=B. Immediate? No.
a3 down-right: b4=B. No.
a3 up-right: b2=B. No.
a3 might not be legal. Wait from a3 down-left doesn't exist. So a3 might have no legal lines.

Check White at b6:
b6 is empty. From White perspective, can White play b6?
Up from b6: b5=B. Immediate? No.
Down from b6: b7=., b8=.. No.
Left: a6=W. Immediate? No.
Right: c6=B. No.
Up-left: a5=B. No.
Up-right: c5=W. Immediate? No.
Down-left: a7=.. No.

Since c5 and d5 are W, there is no B between b6 and e5? Actually from b6: c5(W), d5(W), e5(B). Between b6 and e5, the discs are c5 and d5, which are White, not Black. So no.
What about down: b7=., no.
So b6 is not legal for White.

Wait, but what if Black playing b6 flips things, and then White... Actually b6 might be legal for Black but not for White.

Check White at a7:
a7 right: b7=.. c7=W, but b7 blocks.
Up: a6=W. Immediate? No.
Up-right: b6=. No.
Down-right: b8=. No.
Down: a8=. No.
Up-left: none.
Left: edge.
So a7 not legal for White.

b7 from White perspective:
Right: c7=W. Immediate? No.
Up: b6=.. No.
Down: b8=.. No.
Up-right: c6=B. Immediate? No.
Down-right: c8=.. No.
Up-left: a6=W. Immediate? No.
Down-left: a8=.. No.
So b7 not legal.

a8 from White:
Right: b8=., c8=., d8=W. Hit empty, so no line to d8.
Down: edge.
Up: a7=.. No.
Up-right: b7=.. No.
So no.

b8 from White:
Up-right: c7=W. Immediate? No.
Right: c8=., d8=W. c8 empty blocks.
Up: b7=.. No.
Up-left: a7=.. No.
So no.

c8 from White:
Right: d8=W. Immediate? No.
Up: c7=W. Immediate? No.
Up-right: d7=W. Immediate? No.
Up-left: b7=.. No.
Left: b8=.. No.
So no.

So after g2, White's only legal move is a1? That seems very constrained.
If White plays a1, flips b2 and c3. Then Black might have more moves.

But wait, after g2, Black might have other moves? Actually after Black plays g2, it's White's turn. If White only has a1, then White plays a1. Then it's Black's turn again.

Let's see if Black has any legal moves after White a1.
After g2 + a1:
Black: 28 + ? Black has g2. White plays a1. White flips b2 and c3. So Black loses b2 and c3.
Black now: 28 - 2 = 26 (plus any Black already there? Wait b2 and c3 were Black, now White).
White: 27 + 2 + a1 = 30.
Empty: h1, a3, b6, a7, b7, a8, b8, c8.

Now Black's turn. Legal Black moves from remaining empties.
Check h1 for Black:
Down: h2=B. Immediate? No.
Down-left: g2=B. Immediate? No.
Left: g1=W, f1=W, e1=W, d1=W, c1=W, b1=W, a1=W. a1 is now White. To the left of h1, no Black beyond a1. So no line left because beyond a1 is edge.
Actually from h1 left: g1(W),f1(W),e1(W),d1(W),c1(W),b1(W),a1(W). No Black. So no.
Down-left: g2=B. Immediate? No.
So h1 might not be legal for Black.

a3 for Black:
Up: a2=W, a1=W. Beyond a1 is edge. No Black.
Right: b3=W (since c3 flipped to W by a1). b3 is now W. c3 is W. d3 is B? Wait d3 was flipped by g2 to Black. So from a3: b3(W),c3(W),d3(B). So b3 and c3 flip! d3 is Black. So a3 is legal for Black! Flips b3 and c3.
Also? Down: a4=B. Immediate? No.
Down-right: b4=B. Immediate? No.
Up-right: b2=W (now White), c1=W. Beyond c1 edge. No Black. But b2 is White, c1 is White. No Black beyond.
So a3 flips b3 and c3.

b6 for Black:
Still there. Up-right: c5=W, d5=W, e5=B. So c5,d5 flip. Down-right: c7=W,d7=W,e7=W,f7=W,g7=W,h7=B. So c7-g7 flip. So b6 still legal, flips 7.

a7 for Black: still there. Up: a6=W, a5=B. Up-right: b6=. Hmm b6 is still empty. Wait from a7 up-right is b6. b6 is empty, so no line to c5. Down: a8=. Down-right: b8=. Right: b7=., c7=W... but b7 empty blocks. So a7 still only flips a6 and b6 (up and up-right). Wait b6 is empty, so up-right from a7: b6 is empty. So actually up-right doesn't work because b6 is empty! Let me recheck a7:
a7 up: a6=W, a5=B. Yes.
a7 up-right: b6 is empty. So no.
a7 right: b7 is empty.
So a7 only flips a6.

Wait earlier I said a7 up-right traps b6 because b6=W. But b6 is empty in the original board! Let me check original board.
Row 6: W . B W W B W B
So a6=W, b6=., c6=B...
So b6 is empty! I made a mistake earlier. a7 up-right: b6 is empty, so no line. So a7 only flips a6 (via up to a5). That's 1 disc.

b7 for Black:
Right: c7=W, d7=W, e7=W, f7=W, g7=W, h7=B. So flips c7-g7 (5 discs). Up: b6=.. No. So still 5.

b8 for Black:
Up-right: c7=W, d7=W, e7=W, f7=W, g7=W, h7=B. So flips 5.

c8 for Black:
